machine_approved.method: Shaped with uharfbuzz in both fixture fonts under every config in the unit's set; outlines decomposed with fontTools DecomposingRecordingPen, translated by the cumulative x_advance plus each glyph's x_offset/y_offset, sorted, and compared.

ink_identical.method: Shaped with uharfbuzz in both fixture fonts under every config in the unit's set; outlines decomposed with fontTools DecomposingRecordingPen, translated by the cumulative x_advance plus each glyph's x_offset/y_offset, sorted, and compared.

picture_identical.method: Not ink-identical, but both fixture fonts fill exactly the same pixel-grid cells under every config in the unit's set; only which glyph owns each pixel differs.

junior_equivalent.method: Divergent only under ss10 and placed-ink-identical to the fixture Junior rendering with its letter tracking removed.

classes.title: Join dropped
classes.summary: Letters the old font joined stand apart, for example `·At | ·It` and `·It | ·Et`, where the old font drew `·At ~x~ ·It` and `·It ~x~ ·Et`.
classes.why:
No ruling covers these windows as a whole, so each takes its own verdict. The window differs from the old font without a stylistic set, no junction gains a join, and at least one junction the old font joined now breaks; the leftmost such break names the pair.
Other joins in the word may move as well. A window that also gains a join is listed under the new join instead, because a new join usually causes the changes around it.

classes.title: Same joins and width, letter redrawn or shifted
classes.summary: Joins and width match the old font, but a letter is drawn or placed differently, for example ·I's smaller loop or ·Roe's full top arm after ·Eight.
classes.why:
No ruling covers these windows as a whole, so each takes its own verdict. The window differs from the old font without a stylistic set, every junction joins at the height the old font's did, and the word keeps the old font's width, yet a letter is drawn differently or sits elsewhere: a redrawn stroke, or a letter shifted while the word's width stays the same.
A changed junction the review cannot read stops the build instead of landing here, so every window here keeps its joins and its width.

fixture-identical.title: Fixture class C: looks identical
fixture-identical.summary: A hand-written ink-identical class whose every unit changes its picture, so the build lists those units under a change group.
fixture-identical.why:
Fixture class C: the audit rows of the re-routed units match this class, which says their ink is unchanged.
Each of those units changes its picture, so the build lists it under the change group it shows, and this class keeps no listed class of its own.
